\section[a maratona]{a maratona — marathon}

\label{lesson:PT-C513-maratona}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for volleyball, then the Portuguese for gymnastics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a maratona}
\textbf{a maratona} — \textquotedblleft{}marathon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Correu a maratona em menos de quatro horas.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She ran the marathon in under four hours.}
\end{quote}

Also figurative: \emph{uma maratona de estudo}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{maratona} comes from the Greek place name \emph{Marath\'{\={o}}n} (EtymDB), itself from \emph{márathon} \textquotedblleft{}fennel\textquotedblright{}; the long race recalls a messenger's run from there.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a maratona}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{a maratona}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{a maratona}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for volleyball, then the Portuguese for gymnastics, then say \emph{a maratona} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does a maratona mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Marathon\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o atletismo]{o atletismo — athletics}

\label{lesson:PT-C513-atletismo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for gymnastics, then the Portuguese for marathon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o atletismo}
\textbf{o atletismo} — \textquotedblleft{}athletics\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Na escola, o atletismo é o meu desporto preferido.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{At school, athletics is my favourite sport.}
\end{quote}

An athlete is \emph{um atleta} or \emph{uma atleta}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{atletismo} is built on \emph{atleta}, a learned borrowing through Latin \emph{āthlēta} (Lewis \& Short) from Greek \emph{athlēt\'{\={e}}s} \textquotedblleft{}a competitor\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{âthlos} \textquotedblleft{}a contest\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o atletismo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{o atletismo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o atletismo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for gymnastics, then the Portuguese for marathon, then say \emph{o atletismo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does o atletismo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Athletics\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[o ciclismo]{o ciclismo — cycling}

\label{lesson:PT-C513-ciclismo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for marathon, then the Portuguese for athletics.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o ciclismo}
\textbf{o ciclismo} — \textquotedblleft{}cycling\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O ciclismo é muito popular no verão.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Cycling is very popular in summer.}
\end{quote}

A cyclist is \emph{um ciclista}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ciclismo} is usually traced to French \emph{cyclisme}, built on Greek \emph{kýklos} \textquotedblleft{}a circle, a wheel\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[competir]{competir — to compete}

\label{lesson:PT-C513-competir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for athletics, then the Portuguese for cycling.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: competir}
\textbf{competir} — \textquotedblleft{}to compete\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Cem atletas vão competir na prova.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{A hundred athletes are going to compete in the race.}
\end{quote}

Present: \emph{compito}, \emph{competes}, \emph{compete}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{competir} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{competere} \textquotedblleft{}to come together, to strive for\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built on \emph{petere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o cronómetro]{o cronómetro — stopwatch}

\label{lesson:PT-C513-cronometro}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for cycling, then the Portuguese for to compete.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o cronómetro}
\textbf{o cronómetro} — \textquotedblleft{}stopwatch\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O treinador marcou o tempo com o cronómetro.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The coach timed it with the stopwatch.}
\end{quote}

In Brazil: \emph{cronômetro}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{cronómetro} is a learned coinage from Greek \emph{khrónos} \textquotedblleft{}time\textquotedblright{} and \emph{métron} \textquotedblleft{}measure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{o cronómetro}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Portuguese for cycling, then the Portuguese for to compete, then say \emph{o cronómetro} again
\end{itemize}
